metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Oktober 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.171

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Oktober 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.171
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.171
- Datum: 10.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear H. & M. I would not have believed that in my sixtieth year I would sit
in a little Brasilian village, served by a barefoot black girl and miles
and miles away from all that was formerly my life, books, concerts, friends
conversation. And we feel extremely happy here, the little bungalow with
its large covered terrace (our real living room) has a splendid view
over the mountains and just in front a tiny cafelaus, called „Café
Elegante“ where I can have a delicious café for a halfpenny and enjoy
the company of black mule-drivers. Life is here very cheap and you have
no opportunity to spend, I am working and in my idle hours I play the
master-games of a big chess book - one feels far away from all and
even the war. It was really necessary for us to stabilize for longer time,
we were both frightfully tired, Lotte more by her asthma and myself
by psychic depressions; here in the solitude we hope to get new strength
and alas, we will want much strength. The news from Europe are
so depressing, thanks God not the military ones but those from the
occupied territories - I am afraid, millions will starve while here
all is in peace and full prosperity. There is here now a quite new
nationalism starting, Brasil feels that it will become important
in war and peace, but the people themselves are very nice. We try
to speak Portugiese and it is difficult for me because of my Spanish
which interferes continually. - From Wilmot I have a letter and
I see that he tries to clear my position for next year. Altogether
I regard everything as lost and won't be glad if you can't enjoy
of all as long as it is possible - nobody has an idea what
enormous economic changes this war will produce, also America
will be another country after the war. For you, the younger genera-
tion all this has practical interest, not more for me - in four
years or even in three I will not be able and willing [?] to
adapt myself to the new world, it belongs to your daughter, who
I hope, see and enjoy better times. I wish we could send
you some chocolate or coffee and sugar, which is ridiculously cheap
here but we have not yet found out any possibility. I repeat
my wish, my urgent wish, that you may use all clothes, under-
wear, linen, overcoats and also whatever we have there - it has
not secure to reserve it for years and I am sure I will never use all this. You do
only a favour and you will see that I feel much better with this idea.
I have then to regret of what I shall never see more.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig in violetter Tinte. Der Text am linken Rand wurde quer geschrieben und ist teilweise in den Haupttext integriert.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Kursivschrift. Die wenigen unsicheren Stellen sind durch den Kontext gut erschließbar.
